'''Ann M. Bartuska''' (born August 6, 1953) is an ecologist and biologist. She is a senior advisor at [[Resources for the Future]] and a former Deputy Under Secretary for Research, Education, and Economics (REE) at the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and former USDA Chief Scientist.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.atkinson.cornell.edu/about/people/eab/Bartuska-pop.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617121424/http://www.atkinson.cornell.edu/about/people/eab/Bartuska-pop.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 17, 2018|title=Cornell Atkinson Center|website=www.atkinson.cornell.edu|access-date=2020-02-14}}</ref> 

== Education ==
Bartuska graduated from [[Wilkes University]] in 1975 with a bachelor's degree in [[biology]]. She went on to earn a master's degree in [[botany]] and [[ecology]] from [[Ohio University]] in 1977, and a doctorate in biogeochemistry and ecosystem ecology from [[West Virginia University]] in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wilkes.edu/news/2018/April/kimballlecture_wilkesu_april19.aspx|title=Earth Observations and Public Policy is Focus of Kimball Lecture at Wilkes University on April 19|website=Wilkes University|access-date=2020-02-14}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://esa.org/history/bartuska-a-m/|title=Ann M. Bartuska|website=esa.org|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> Her dissertation, titled ''Detrital processes in a black locust reforested surface mine compared to a sugar maple dominated mixed hardwood stand,'' was completed under adviser, Dr. Gerald E. Lang.<ref name=":1" />  Her research has focused on ecosystems processes in [[Landscape|landscapes]] disturbed by [[coal mining]]. She is married to Dr. Mark R. Walbridge, Chair of the Department of Biology at West Virginia University.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|date=April 2003|title=Ann Bartuska, President of the Ecological Society of America, 2002-2003|url=https://www.esa.org/history/biogr/Bartuska_AMpb.pdf|journal=Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America|volume=99|issue=2 |pages=57|doi=10.1890/0012-9623(2003)84[57:ABPOTE]2.0.CO;2 |bibcode=2003BuESA..84...57. }}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1982 until 1989, Bartuska managed research, development, and assessment programs associated with the effects of [[acid rain]] and [[air pollution]], first for [[North Carolina State University]] and then under the [[United States Forest Service]].  Both projects fell under the [[National Acid Precipitation Assessment Program]].<ref name=":2" />  In 1989 she was named Assistant Station Director for Continuing Research at the [[Southern Research Station|Southeastern Forest Experiment Station]]; while there, she was responsible for research in both [[Florida]] and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].<ref name=":2" />  She later joined the staff of Forest Environment Research at the Forest Service's Washington Office in 1991 as a Wetlands Specialist with the responsibility of developing a National Wetlands Research Program.<ref name=":2" />  In 1992, when the Ecosystem Management staff was created, she was named the first head.<ref name=":2" /> Bartuska spent a year in 1993 as the Forest Service Liaison to the National Biological Survey of the U.S. Department of Interior and in October 1994 became director of Forest Health Protection for the Forest Service.

In January 1999, Bartuska was named Director of Forest Management, of which she was the first woman and first ecologist to hold the position.<ref name=":2" />   She continued on as director, when Forest Management and Range Management were merged.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.webpages.uidaho.edu/winr/bartuska.htm|title=bartuska.htm|website=www.webpages.uidaho.edu|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>  Bartuska left the Forest Service in 2001 to become the executive director of [[The Nature Conservancy|The Nature Conservancy's Invasive Species Initiative]], and she remained there until 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.agci.org/redhen/contact/1614|title=Ann Bartuska|website=Aspen Global Change Institute|access-date=2020-02-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.ucr.edu/2287|title=UCR Newsroom: Climate Change, Bark Beetles, Environmental Markets and Sustainability|website=newsroom.ucr.edu|access-date=2020-02-14}}</ref>  She returned to the Forest Service as Deputy Chief for Research and Development in 2004 and from January to October 2009 served as acting Deputy Undersecretary for Natural Resources and Environment.<ref name=":3" />  In 2010 she joined the USDA's Research, Education, and Economics (REE) mission area, where she was Deputy Under Secretary.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agci.org/redhen/contact/1614|title=Ann Bartuska {{!}} Aspen Global Change Institute|website=www.agci.org|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> 
Her responsibilities included oversight over four agencies which support the REE mission: [[Agricultural Research Service]] (ARS - which includes the [[United States National Agricultural Library|National Agricultural Library]] and [[United States National Arboretum|National Arboretum]]), [[National Institute of Food and Agriculture]] (NIFA), [[Economic Research Service]] (ERS), and [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]] (NASS).

Ann Bartuska was named chair of the Subcommittee on [[U.S. Global Change Research Program|Global Change Research]] (SGCR) by Dr. Tamara Dickinson, Principal Assistant Director for Environment and Energy at the [[Office of Science and Technology Policy|White House Office of Science and Technology Policy]] in 2016, of which she previously served as vice-chair. The group was created and is responsible for, meeting the requirement of the [[Global Change Research Act of 1990]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.globalchange.gov/news/ann-bartuska-usda-appointed-sgcr-chair|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826173557/http://www.globalchange.gov/news/ann-bartuska-usda-appointed-sgcr-chair|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 26, 2016|title=Ann Bartuska of USDA Appointed SGCR Chair|website=GlobalChange.gov|language=en|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>  In 2017, Bartuska joined the non-profit, [[Resources for the Future]] (RFF), as vice president of the newly formed program on Land, Water, and Nature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.resourcesmag.org/common-resources/new-rff-vice-president-for-land-water-and-nature-ann-m-bartuska/|title=New RFF Vice President for Land, Water, and Nature: Ann M. Bartuska|website=Resources for the Future|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>  She currently serves as a senior adviser to RFF, focused on natural resources and forestry with special consideration of natural climate solutions through forest and agricultural lands.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rff.org/people/ann-m-bartuska/|title=Ann M. Bartuska|website=Resources for the Future|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>

== Memberships and legacy ==
Bartuska was vice president for public affairs at the [[Ecological Society of America]] from 1996 to 1999 and president of the society from 2003–2004.<ref name=":2" /> She was a co-chair of the Science and Technology for Sustainability Roundtable of the National Academies,  served on the Board of the Council of Science Society Presidents, and is a member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]](AAAS) and [[Society for Advancement of Chicanos and Native Americans in Science|Society for the Advancement of Chicanos and Native American in Science]] (SACNAS).<ref name=":3" />  Bartuska has also served on the advisory board of the [[National Science Foundation]] and on the External Advisory Board for the Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability.<ref name=":0" /> She served as co-chair of the Ecological Systems subcommittee of the Committee on Environment, Natural Resources, and Sustainability of the White House National Science and Technology Council.  She was also a part of the [https://sites.nationalacademies.org/PGA/sustainability/PGA_048724 Sustainability Roundtable of the National Academy of Sciences.]<ref name=":4" /> She was one of the inaugural Fellows of the Ecological Society of America, elected in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESA Fellows |url=https://esa.org/about/awards/fellows-program/esa-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref>
